item.title: Alpine Glaciologists Deploy Low-Power Radar Stakes to Track Winter Melt Pockets
item.description:
INNSBRUCK — Glaciologists monitoring upper Alpine catchment basins have anchored forty low-power ground-penetrating radar stakes directly into bedrock ridges above 3,200 meters, giving downstream hydrologists real-time visibility into sub-surface winter melt pockets.

Satellite altimetry measures total snow height well, yet misses hidden liquid water pooling beneath frozen surface crusts during unseasonal mid-winter thaws.

Early Warnings for Downstream Reservoirs

Hydroelectric operators and valley flood boards now receive hourly dielectric readings over long-range radio links, sharpening spring runoff forecasts weeks before snowpack collapse begins.
